metadata.scope: Gierahn 2017 Seq-Well implementation as depicted; exclude later S3 refinements.
metadata.copy_boundary: JSON inspection copy; native byte hashes refer to archived original files, not this serialization.

checks.rationale: The decomposition covers every in-scope transformation: cell confinement, joint cell/bead loading and sealing, lysis with poly(A) capture, then bead recovery and cDNA-library preparation. The poly(A) icon identifies the cellular target rather than an RNA-extraction action. Six material boundaries preserve intact cells, sealed compartments, captured RNA and the physical library. The two-input sealing operation is a genuine depicted combination, not independent branches. Recovery and preparation can remain one composite block because the source shows one retained route to one library. No isolated RNA fractions, unshown sequencing data or neighboring workflows are invented.

checks.rationale: Accept at the declared schematic/2017 implementation scope. Independent image inspection and registered primary architecture passages support all six material States, four local Operations, nine material Flows, their labels/properties and Seq-Well applicability. Every in-scope action and the joint loading interface are represented; no independent branch is collapsed. Cell-first loading is expressly supported by the original PBMC implementation, and recovery precedes bulk reverse transcription in the actual composite operation and output context, so no contradictory order requires a Correction. The endpoint is a physical barcoded cDNA library representing captured poly(A) mRNA through transcript sequence, cell barcode and UMI, with occupancy/isolation limitations retained. Both supplied reference leads are assessed as the same identified, content-checked Seq-Well paper. No consequential unsupported assertion or architecture question remains; unshown execution details are outside scope.
